messages:
maya: Heads-up: tenant-82 flipped to v2 via soft-fallback and we saw a spike in 429s and a flurry of support tickets. Console shows a deprecating badge but it's not clear which route actually served traffic. Anyone seen this pattern before?

sam: Which endpoint? global routing or the mobile proxy?

maya: Mobile proxy -> they still send `x-client-version: 1.0` but we routed to v2 because v1 pool was throttled.

ian: Saw something similar last month when header negotiation fell back. Logs show `negotiation=soft-fallback served=v2 requested=v1 seq_len=512`.

maya: The main question: for quota/billing/console UX, do we attribute usage to the requested version or the served version? Tenants are confused when console shows "deprecating" but metrics jump.

ben: For billing transparency, my vote is attribute to the requested version. Tenants requested v1, they should see cost/quota consumption there. Otherwise invoices look wrong.

gina: From infra + cost accuracy we should also track what actually ran. v2 models (esp quantized variants) have different unit costs. We need both sides.

maya: Proposal: add two columns in the console traffic table: `requested_version` and `served_version`. Tooltip explains billing rule (requested by default) and shows an engineering breakdown. Add a small "why am I being charged" link.

sam: Agree. Also need telemetry fields: `compat.requested_version`, `compat.served_version`, `compat.fallback_reason`.

deploy-bot: Canary: console staging rollout for the dual-column experiment started at 2024-11-03 08:12 UTC (cohort=5%).

ian: Edge-case: if fallback uses a smaller quantized v2 variant to meet latency, the cost per token is lower but compute path differs. We need a cost-attribution mapping: map served_variant -> cost_bucket.

ben: +1 on mapping table. Also suggest a preview API/webhook so tenants can see predicted billing delta if they opt-in before we flip attribution.

gina: Rollout sequence suggestion: 1) define telemetry schema and routing policy doc; 2) implement backend attribution; 3) expose columns in console with opt-in preview; 4) announce with migration guidance. Start at 5% tenants.

sam: I'll open the telemetry PR and include event examples. Ping me if you want to pair on schema. Example event: `{ "tenant": "82", "requested_version": "v1", "served_version": "v2-small-q4", "tokens": 12345 }`.

maya: I'll draft the console copy and the tooltip text. Ben can you own billing/legal note?

ben: On it. One more UI question: should the "deprecation" badge auto-dismiss after tenant explicitly pins to older version? I think yes, with an audit log entry.

ian: We should also add an escape hatch: allow console pin to old version for up to 7 days and emit an audit event: `compat.pin: { owner, until, reason }`.

gina: Also add a small telemetry sampler for these pin actions so we can measure how many tenants actually rely on the escape hatch.

maya: Ok action items I/O: 1) sam telemetry PR; 2) ian mapping table + escape-hatch API; 3) ben billing note + legal; 4) maya console copy + tooltip; 5) gina rollout doc. I'll link the spec: https://go.redwood/specs/compat-attribution (placeholder).

sam: FYI I correlated the 429 spike with quota-smoothing change at 07:58 — adding to incident timeline.

gina: Great. I'll start the rollout playbook and list the 5% cohorts.

maya: Thanks all. We'll sync tomorrow 10am PT to confirm telemetry fields and cohort IDs.

ben: :thumbsup:

ian: :+1:

maya: Filing follow-ups in the board.
